body:
Tested locally on all GUI demos, it works as expected. Code looks good to me.

I couldn't spot any regressions in previous/next focus behavior.

Note that this PR does not affect left/top/right/bottom neighbor determination when navigating with the arrow keys or d-pad. It's still broken out of the box on the Drag and Drop demo:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9c5ce8a-6160-45fb-8ce0-00b4abe816e7

This can be addressed by assigning explicit neighbors to all buttons on the edges (only the one at the center doesn't need explicit neighbors).

Tests on the Control Gallery demo on the latest revision of this PR:

### Legacy

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5aee28c-b788-4473-9825-687a74815f37

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/011b6505-3abd-4225-9c0d-4726b5c94757

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c52a68e-5415-4f0d-a475-daf1d5579b03

### Balloon

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d770042-7e7b-45bd-878f-51e2efe02fa0

Overall, it's better in Balloon but there is still one case where it unexpectedly goes to the left column's CheckButton while pressing <kbd>Down</kbd> (while the HSlider in the middle column is focused).

Tested with Rift Riff and the web project @rsubtil put together, and this resolved all my gripes with automatic navigation. Didn't look at the code.

Now that there is a project setting for this, I wonder whether we should name this in such a way that it's limitations are also clear and that a potential variation to this algorithm could then be named logically alongside the current balloon algorithm. In particular, I'm thinking about a variation of the balloon algorithm that is less '4-directional' and more 'any direction' – and thus potentially more intuitive with joystick controls or UI's that desire diagonal navigation (like some of the skill trees in the web project). @rsubtil what do you think: should such an improvement be a different algorithm, or an improvement to the one you already made?

The code looks mostly fine.
Didn't test.
Code looks good, and new algo seems to be more intuitive in all cases I have tested.
